# Job Safety Analysis and Work Plan: High-Bay Lighting Retrofit
Project: Apex Logistics Facility B - High-Bay LED Upgrade
Date: 03/18/2026
Supervisor: Marcus Vance (Master Electrician, Lic #EC-44910)

## Equipment and Staging Specifications
| Item | Specification | Rating / Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile Scaffolding Unit | Steel tubular frame, 5 ft x 7 ft base | ANSI A10.8 Type I |
| Maximum Working Platform Height | 16 ft above finished floor (AFF) | Outriggers engaged |
| Fixture Weight | 150W LED High-Bay (Model HB-4) | 18 lb each |
| Branch Circuit | 277V single-phase, 20A breaker | Circuit H-14 |

## Scaffolding Setup and Stability
- The mobile scaffold base is 5 ft wide by 7 ft long.
- Scaffold height is configured to a platform level of 16 ft AFF with base-to-height ratio stabilised using four outriggers.
- Working platform is fully planked with nominal 2-inch wood scaffolding grade lumber and equipped with top rails at 42 inches AFF and midrails.
- To relocate the unit along the aisle, crew members may ride the rolling scaffold between bays provided travel speed remains walking pace.

## Circuit Load Evaluation
- The existing circuit H-14 powers 277V luminaires using 12 AWG THHN copper conductors on a standard 20A branch breaker.
- Total planned replacement fixtures on Circuit H-14: 24 luminaires at 150W each.
- Total connected operating load across all 24 fixtures equals 4,200 watts.
- At 277V, total steady-state continuous draw is 13.0 amps, which remains below the 16A continuous threshold (80% of 20A circuit rating).

## Fall Protection and Ladder Access
- Access to the scaffold platform is provided via an attached internal ladder unit.
- When climbing the ladder to the scaffold deck, workers must maintain two points of contact at all times.
- Personal fall arrest systems (PFAS) with full-body harness and 6 ft energy-absorbing lanyards are required when working outside guardrails.

errors.quote: crew members may ride the rolling scaffold between bays
errors.explanation: OSHA 1926.452(w)(6) prohibits employees from riding on scaffolds unless specific design criteria are met, and manual pushing while workers are on top violates standard safety rules.
errors.fix: crew members must dismount the scaffold before moving it between bays

errors.quote: Total connected operating load across all 24 fixtures equals 4,200 watts.
errors.explanation: 24 fixtures multiplied by 150 watts each equals 3,600 watts, not 4,200 watts.
errors.fix: Total connected operating load across all 24 fixtures equals 3,600 watts.

errors.quote: workers must maintain two points of contact at all times.
errors.explanation: Standard safety rules and basic trade knowledge require three points of contact (two hands and a foot, or two feet and a hand) while climbing a ladder, not two.
errors.fix: workers must maintain three points of contact at all times.
